subject: P0: Heliotrope — westus3 throughput & 5xx floodgate (exec visibility requested)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heliotrope.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@heliotrope.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: P0: High error rate & throughput collapse in westus3

Markus / Marissa —

We're seeing a full outage on our production write tier routed to westus3 starting ~08:45 PT. Traffic that normally sits at ~12k qps for our ingestion cluster dropped to ~1.2k and 30% of requests return 5xx (502/504). Latency tail climbed to >4s for user-facing endpoints. This started right after a routine autoscaler window and appears to have affected only westus3 routing.

Impact: several batch jobs failed, downstream ML pipelines backlogged, a spike in customer tickets. We attempted to fail traffic to eastus2 but saw mixed behavior — some requests failed fast, some retried into a degraded path.

We need:
- Immediate bridge with your ops/engineers.
- Cross-region steering enabled now.
- Visibility on whether this is capacity, config, or control-plane decisioning.

I'm attaching a short sample of failed request IDs and a small trace (attached). We are prepared to join a bridge immediately. This is materially impacting our SLAs — please treat as P0.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform
Heliotrope AI

Attachments: heliotrope_fail_samples.txt, sample_trace_08-50.json

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heliotrope.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P0: High error rate & throughput collapse in westus3

Liam —

Thank you for the heads up and the samples. I'm escalating this now to our SRE and routing leads and we've stood up a P0 bridge (link below). Marissa is joining as the primary engineering contact.

Immediate actions we're initiating:
- Opened incident PD-9982 and connected ops (bridge link below).
- Activating cross-region steering to route new ingestion traffic to eastus2 as a soft-failover while preserving read locality.
- Pulling recent autoscaler events / K/V cache metrics for westus3; requesting trace snapshot from your sample IDs.

Can you confirm whether any customer-side retries were disabled? Also please share the most recent IAM token TTLs if possible — we're suspicious of an aggressive connection churn pattern.

Bridge: https://pager.redwood.com/incident/PD-9982
Support ticket: https://support.redwood.com/ticket/HLT-4621

On the call now: Marissa, Hannah, Connor, Rishi. We'll update every 30 minutes and aim for a mitigation within the hour.

—Markus Klein
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: HelioTrope westus3 initial triage (trace + hypothesis)

Quick summary of what we see from our side after ingesting the samples:
- Trace snapshots (attached) show bursts of downstream KV cache misses and an abnormal number of session reconnects at the westus3 gateway layer between 08:42–08:48 PT.
- The autoscaler fired but did not attach new GPU serving instances for a subset of slots due to a threshold-evaluation bug in the scale-authorization flow (we have a patch in staging).
- When the steering attempted failover, a subset of write requests were routed to nodes that had stale KV cache state causing synchronous recompute and 5xx to surface.

Immediate recommended mitigation (applied in this order):
1) Soft-steer new ingestion traffic to eastus2 (already in progress).
2) Temporarily lower the autoscaler threshold and trigger a controlled attach for westus3 pools to stabilize pending capacity.
3) Flush/refresh KV cache on the impacted westus3 serving pools in a rolling fashion to avoid global cold-start.

I've attached trace_snapshot_1130.json with flagged spans and a short checklist. If we can get a confirmation to proceed with cache roll and scale-down/attach, we'll execute now.

Attachments: trace_snapshot_1130.json (internal)

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heliotrope.ai>, SaaS Ops <ops@heliotrope.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Mitigation in flight + visibility (Heliotrope P0)

Liam —

Update from the bridge and actions we've taken so far:
- Cross-region steering to eastus2 has been engaged for write-heavy ingestion routes. We're seeing a progressive lift in throughput and a drop in 5xx rates for the re-routed traffic.
- We've lowered the autoscaler sensitivity and initiated an emergency attach for 4 additional serving slots in westus3 to absorb retry storms.
- Marissa's team executed a controlled KV cache refresh on the most impacted pools; that reduced synchronous recompute on subsequent requests.

I've attached a short latency/RTT snapshot showing the before/after from 08:40–11:20 PT. Early signals are positive but we will keep the steer active until we confirm stable tail latency for 30m.

We appreciate the quick samples you provided — they were essential. As a next step, please confirm any downstream business cutoffs we should be aware of (billing window, critical customers hitting us between 12:00–13:00). We will also start a post-incident credit calculation and share a proposal by EOD.

Attachments: rtt_dashboard.png

—Markus Klein
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heliotrope.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: ops@heliotrope.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mitigation in flight + visibility (Heliotrope P0)

Markus —

Thanks for the rapid response and the mitigation. We can confirm traffic shifted and most ingestion succeeded via eastus2; system health is improved versus the peak. We still see intermittent retries (two-minute windows) and one large customer reported delayed processing that affected a late-night pipeline run.

We need two things now:
1) A written estimate of customer impact (% of failed/latency-impacted ingestion) and proposed credit (SLA) model.
2) An exec-level readout with Redwood leadership — our CFO and Head of Ops want to understand the root cause and remediation timeline before we finalize our month-end reconciliation.

Can you propose a time for a 30-min exec sync today or tomorrow morning?

Appreciate the team.

—Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform, Heliotrope AI

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T14:58:00-08:00
Subject: Exec sync & proposed near-term commercial relief (Heliotrope P0)

Team —

Per Liam's ask, escalating for exec visibility. Recommend we offer a one-time good-faith credit equivalent to 30% of ingestion over the affected 2-hour window and schedule a joint executive readout with Heliotrope tomorrow 10:00 PT. Rationale: material customer impact, cost to Heliotrope, and our transparent mitigation timeline.

Action items:
- Markus: please prepare a short two-slide executive brief (impact numbers + what went wrong).
- Marissa / Rishi: finalize a short technical RCA draft (root cause = autoscaler scale-auth bug + stale KV state behavior).
- Hannah / Connor: propose immediate follow-ups to prevent recurrence (automated pre-attach, guardrail on steer decisioning).
- Finance ops (I'll loop separately): prepare a credit memo for 30% of impacted ingestion for the 08:40–10:40 PT window under ticket HLT-4621.

Let's keep the tone constructive; we want to preserve the relationship and move quickly to a postmortem and remediation plan.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
